title: One member per email
statement: Two members MUST NOT share an email address (an email address being trimmed and in lower case, TL-VO02-C02).

title: A tool needing repair stays so until it is marked repaired
statement: A tool whose condition is `needs_repair` MUST keep that condition and its damage report until a librarian marks it repaired. Nothing else sets it back to `good`: a return that records the condition as `good` does not clear damage reported while the tool was on loan. A second damage report while the tool needs repair MUST be refused, so the first report stands.

title: A tool is lent to one member at a time
statement: No two active loans MAY name the same tool. A tool can be lent again once its loan is returned.

title: A loan is due 14 calendar days after it starts
statement: A loan's due date MUST be the date it starts plus 14 calendar days, both dates taken in the library's time zone (TL-LEND-DS01). A renewal moves it on 14 more calendar days from the due date it had (TL-LEND-INV07). The due date is a date (YYYY-MM-DD), not a time: it is stored and shown that way, and the loan is due by the end of that day. For example, a loan started at 23:30 on 2 March in New York (04:30 on 3 March in UTC) is due on 16 March, and on 30 March once renewed.

title: A loan is returned once
statement: A loan MUST be returned at most once. Once returned, its return time, condition and note MUST NOT change.

title: A returned loan records its return
statement: A returned loan MUST record the time of return and the tool's condition as found by the librarian, and MAY record a note.

title: A loan is renewed at most once
statement: A loan MUST be renewed at most once. A renewal moves its due date on 14 calendar days from the due date it had (TL-LEND-INV04); a second renewal of the same loan MUST be refused.

title: A loan's member is reminded at most once
statement: The library MUST remind a loan's member that it is due at most once, even after a renewal moves the due date. A returned loan MUST NOT be reminded.
